note.note:
History:
• Chief complaint: 2-day history of mid-lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain.  
• Course: Constant over 48 h; no prior similar episodes.  
• Associated symptoms: Feeling hot/sweaty, mild nausea (no vomiting), slight pink-tinged urine, ↑ urinary frequency, ↑ thirst.  
• Bowel history: Constipated last week; stools now normal; last bowel movement 2 h before call, normal, no blood.  
• Urinary history: No dysuria; no flank/back pain; urine occasionally pink.  
• Gynecologic: Regular periods; no inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding; no vaginal discharge; had contraceptive implant removed 1 y ago.  
• Constitutional: No measured fever (home temp 37 °C); no rigors.  
• Triggers/alleviating factors: None described.  
• Travel: No recent travel.  
• Social: Lives with parents; non-smoker; alcohol ~1 beer on 4 days/week.  
• Family history: Mother – early breast cancer.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Surgical/gynecologic: Contraceptive implant removed 1 y ago.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).  
• Medications: None regular; no OTC drugs.  

Physical Examination:
• Remote consultation; no in-person exam performed.  
• Reported vitals: Home oral temperature 37 °C one hour prior.  
• General appearance, abdomen, GU exam: Not recorded.  

Impression:
Likely acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection) based on suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and hematuria in an afebrile young woman.  
DDx also considered by clinician/AI (consistent with history):  
1. Urolithiasis – hematuria + abdominal pain but pain mild, no colic.  
2. Early appendicitis – less likely; urinary findings not explained.  

Management Plan:
• Prescribed 3-day course of oral antibiotics for presumed UTI (drug and dose/route/frequency not documented beyond “twice a day for three days”).  
• Sent prescription to patient’s nominated pharmacy.  
• Safety-net advice: Seek immediate review if pain worsens, fever develops, back/flank pain arises, new symptoms occur, or symptoms recur after treatment.  
• Advised to start medication as soon as collected.  
• Follow-up: Contact service if no improvement or symptom recurrence; possible face-to-face exam may be required.  

Patient Summary:
Young woman with 2-day suprapubic pain, frequency, and pink urine was assessed remotely; findings are most consistent with uncomplicated cystitis. Oral antibiotics supplied; patient instructed to monitor and seek review for any deterioration.  

Key Takeaways:
• Begin the prescribed antibiotic twice daily for 3 days as soon as collected.  
• If pain, fever, or back pain develops—or if no improvement—contact the clinic immediately.  
• Maintain hydration; return if symptoms recur.  

Next Steps:
• Pick up antibiotic from nominated pharmacy today.  
• Re-evaluation if no improvement within 48–72 h or sooner if red-flag symptoms appear.  
• Consider urine dip, culture, or in-person exam if symptoms persist or recur.  

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Objective vitals (BP, HR, RR), abdominal/GU physical exam, urine dipstick/culture, pregnancy test, detailed antibiotic name/dose.  
• Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional incomplete sentences but clinical details understandable.
